title: A2A 101
subtitle: The Agent2Agent protocol, from its purpose to each request and response
summary: How one agent gives work to another agent that it cannot see inside. Each request, response, and stream event in this manual comes from a recorded run.
audience: You are an engineer who has built an agent that calls tools or a model API. You know HTTP and JSON. You have not read the A2A specification.
outcomes: Read an agent card and say what the agent offers, how to reach it, and what it requires before you send anything.
Predict which state a task is in at any point of a run, and what a client is allowed to do next.
Choose between a blocking call, polling, streaming, and push notifications for a given job.
Read any A2A request, response, or stream frame line by line, in either JSON binding.
Name the errors a client must handle and the rules a server can break without noticing.

plate.title: One planner, three remote agents
plate.caption: The planner reads three cards and delegates three tasks: one completes at once, one after a question, and one after an operator approves. Lanes run top to bottom in the order of capture/out/19-planner.log, and ids are shortened to 8 characters.

parts.title: The Protocol on One Page
parts.thesis: A2A standardizes how one agent finds another agent, gives it work, and follows that work, and it leaves the agent itself out of scope.

parts.title: AgentCard
parts.thesis: Before a client sends a message, the AgentCard tells it what the agent offers, where to reach it, and what it requires.

parts.title: Data Model
parts.thesis: Every A2A exchange is built from five objects: Message, Part, Artifact, Task, and the contextId that groups tasks.

parts.title: Operations
parts.thesis: Eleven operations create, read, cancel, and follow tasks, and each one has rules that a client must know before it calls.

parts.title: Bindings
parts.thesis: The same operations travel over JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, and gRPC, with two headers and one error model shared by all three.

parts.title: Security and Extensions
parts.thesis: The card declares how to authenticate and which extensions apply, and the specification lists what each side must check.

parts.title: Implementing A2A
parts.thesis: A client and a server follow the rules of the earlier parts, and the official test kit checks the server against them.
